passage: Understanding the media and advertising is essential for every citizen. Many people ask, why do companies spend so much money on advertisements? While ads do inform us about products, their primary goal is to persuade us to buy specific brands, often creating a desire for products we might not actually need. A common myth is that expensive, branded items are always superior in quality to unbranded ones, but this is often just a result of clever marketing. Furthermore, we must consider how media functions. Some believe that because a news channel is independent, it must be perfectly objective. However, all media outlets have their own perspectives and interests, meaning no report is entirely free from bias. Another misconception is that we should blindly trust whatever the media highlights as important. In reality, the media chooses what to cover based on their own priorities, and we must critically evaluate their stories rather than accepting them as absolute truth. By questioning the motives behind advertisements and news reports, we can become more informed citizens who make choices based on facts rather than influence. Remember, media and advertising are powerful tools that shape our opinions, so staying alert is your best defense against manipulation.

items.evidence: While ads do inform us about products, their primary goal is to persuade us to buy specific brands, often creating a desire for products we might not actually need.
items.q: Why does a soap company spend so much money on TV advertisements?
options: To make people want to buy its brand
To simply inform people about a new soap
To prove its soap is the very best
To show people what they truly need
items.explain: Ads give some information, but their main aim is to persuade us to buy a particular brand.

wrong.why: thinks ads are only meant to inform
thinks an ad proves a brand is best
reverses the point that ads create desire for things we may not need

items.evidence: A common myth is that expensive, branded items are always superior in quality to unbranded ones, but this is often just a result of clever marketing.
items.q: Many people think a costly branded bag is better than an unbranded one. What often causes this belief?
options: Smart advertising that builds the brand's image
Superior quality, as costly brands are always better
Ads that only share facts about new products
News reports that fairly test every brand
items.explain: The belief that branded goods are always better often comes from clever marketing, not real quality.

wrong.why: believes expensive brands are always better quality
assumes the media checks products without bias

items.evidence: However, all media outlets have their own perspectives and interests, meaning no report is entirely free from bias.
items.q: A news channel is independent. What will its news reports still contain?
options: Some bias from the channel's own interests
No bias at all, since nobody controls it
Only the stories that truly matter to us
Bias only in the adverts it shows
items.explain: Every media outlet has its own views and interests, so no report is fully free from bias.

wrong.why: thinks the media shows only what is important
limits bias to ads instead of all reports

items.evidence: In reality, the media chooses what to cover based on their own priorities, and we must critically evaluate their stories rather than accepting them as absolute truth.
items.q: A channel shows one story all day as the most important news. What should a careful viewer do?
options: Judge it, as channels pick stories for their own reasons
Believe it, since media shows what truly matters
Ignore it, since all news stories are false
Trust it fully, since the channel is independent
items.explain: Media picks stories by its own priorities, so we should think carefully, not accept them as absolute truth.

wrong.why: believes whatever the media highlights is important
over-generalises checking into thinking all news is false
thinks an independent channel tells the absolute truth

items.evidence: By questioning the motives behind advertisements and news reports, we can become more informed citizens who make choices based on facts rather than influence.
items.q: How does questioning the motives behind ads and news help us as citizens?
options: We make choices from facts, not from persuasion
We buy the brands that have the best ads
We learn to pick costly brands every time
We learn to fully trust independent channels
items.explain: Questioning motives makes us informed citizens who choose based on facts rather than influence.

wrong.why: thinks a liked ad means the brand is best
thinks expensive brands are always better
thinks independent channels are always true
